title: Special Weather Statement
location: Glades

details.description:
At 400 PM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists were tracking
a strong thunderstorm capable of producing a landspout near Brighton
Seminole Reservation, or near Lakeport, moving southwest at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Landspouts and wind gusts of 45 to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Minor damage to outdoor objects is possible. Gusty winds
could knock down tree limbs and blow around unsecured
objects.

Locations impacted include...
Lakeport and Brighton Seminole Reservation.
details.instruction:
This activity was also developing in an environment favorable for the
formation of funnel clouds. Stay tuned to NOAA weather radio and
local media for additional updates and possible warnings.

Persons participating in outdoor activities should seek sturdy
shelter until this storm passes. Open shelters found in parks,
beaches, or golf courses offer no protection from the dangers of
lightning.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

title: Flash Flood Warning
location: Catron, NM

details.description:
FFWABQ

The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Sacaton and Hummingbird burn scars in...
South Central Catron County in west central New Mexico...

* Until 445 PM MDT.

* At 142 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Sacaton and Hummingbird Burn Scars. Between 0.5
and 0.75 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
0.5 to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will impact Willow Creek Canyon
along Willow Creek Road. The debris flow can consist of rock, mud,
vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Sacaton and Hummingbird
Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Sacaton and Hummingbird Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of South Central Catron County.
details.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks, streams and ditches in
the Sacaton and Hummingbird Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also
be anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away
in places. If you encounter flood waters, climb to safety.

title: Extreme Heat Warning
location: Indian Wells Valley; Mojave Desert

details.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures between
108 to 112 degrees and low temperatures between 75 to 83 degrees.

* WHERE...Indian Wells Valley and Mojave Desert.

* WHEN...Until 9 PM PDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
details.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Stay cool, stay hydrated, stay informed.

title: Flood Warning
location: Dimmit, TX

details.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Asherton affecting Dimmit County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Asherton.

* WHEN...Until early Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 27.0 feet, Major widespread lowland flooding cuts off
and potentially drowns livestock above Uvalde to below Tilden.
Most secondary roads and low bridges near the river flood. Flow is
within a foot of the bottom of the Farm to Market 190 bridge and
the approaches are flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:30 PM CDT Friday the stage was 26.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours
ending at 1:30 PM CDT Friday was 27.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
early Sunday morning and continue falling to 9.7 feet early
Wednesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 20.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of
27.0 feet on 01/03/1985.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
details.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning by 830 AM CDT.

title: Flash Flood Warning
location: Coconino, AZ

details.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The North Canyon Wash Basin downstream of the Dragon Bravo Fire
scar in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...
This includes State Route 67 between mile markers 608 and 610. This
includes the Colorado River between river miles 17 and 21, near
river mile 32 and between river miles 37 and 47.

* Until 315 PM MST /415 PM MDT/.

* At 1218 PM MST /118 PM MDT/, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms
producing heavy rain over the North Canyon Wash Basin downstream of
the Dragon Bravo Fire scar. Between 0.5 and 1.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the North Canyon Wash Basin
downstream of the Dragon Bravo Fire scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
North Canyon Wash Basin downstream of the Dragon Bravo
Fire scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Saddle Mountain Wilderness, Bert Loper's Boat, Royal Arches, Triple
Alcoves, Point Hansbrough, Anasazi Foot Bridge and North Rim
Entrance Station.

This includes the following highways...
State Route 67 between mile markers 609 and 610. the Colorado River
between river miles 17 and 21...and near river mile 32...and between
river miles 37 and 47.

House Rock Camp Site, 18 Mile Wash Camp Site, 18 Mile Ledges Camp
Site, Upper North Canyon Camp Site, Lower North Canyon Camp Site,
South Canyon Camp Site, Tatahatso Wash Camp Site, Tatahatso Camp
Site, Above Martha's Camp Site, Martha's Camp Site, Redbud Alcove
Camp Site, MCD Site Camp Site, Upper Buck Farm Camp Site, Buck Farm
Camp Site, Below Buck Farm Camp Site, Loper's Boat Camp Site, Royal
Arches Camp Site, Anasazi Bridge Camp Site, Above Willie Taylor Camp
Site, Willie Taylor Camp Site, Triple Alcoves Camp Site, Duck N Quack
Camp Site, Upper Saddle Camp Site and Lower Saddle Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
"Bert's Canyon", Colorado River, South Canyon, Bright Angel Creek,
Buck Farm Canyon, "19- Mile Canyon", Hanaa Ninadzidzahi, "Redbud
Alcove", North Canyon Wash, House Rock Wash, Saddle Canyon, "18-
Mile Wash", Tatahatso Wash and North Canyon.
details.instruction:
Flash flooding is occurring or imminent downstream of the Dragon
Bravo Fire scar. Severe debris flow are expected across roads and in
